tables.claim: 1. Table 1, Risk-based prioritisation, Acute event rate (%): 12.3 (95% CI: 11.9–12.7)
tables.explanation: Execution stage: The paper claims a risk-based prioritization acute event rate of 12.3% (95% CI: 11.9–12.7). Execution of the code with all tested configurations (various seeds and patient counts) produces rates consistently in the range 10.47–11.36%, well below the claimed 12.3%. The data generation formula (base_rate = 0.05 + 0.02*comorbidity + 0.01*prior_ed) with Poisson(2) comorbidities and Poisson(1) ED visits cannot produce 12.3% average rates. The code and data structure match the paper's description, but the reported numbers conflict with actual execution results.
tables.evidence: Existing synthetic_data.csv (36,963 rows): overall acute_event rate = 10.88%, per-state range 10.47-11.09%. Generated with 5000 patients, seed 42: overall rate = 10.85%, per-state range 10.36-11.36%. Tested seeds 0,1,42,123 and patient counts 2000,5000,10000: all rates in range 10.47-11.36%, none approaching 12.3%. | Code: fcaf_rl_code/run_experiment.py:92 (baseline_rate = test_df['acute_event'].mean()); fcaf_rl_code/synthetic_data_generation.py:83 (base_rate = 0.05 + 0.02 * comorbidity_count + 0.01 * prior_ed_visits)
